modules._comment: DN-70: 9th compliance module, first cybersecurity/operational-resilience-focused one - DORA (Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, Digital Operational Resilience Act). Directly applicable EU Regulation (no national transposition), in force since 17 Jan 2025, covering ~20 types of financial entities. Art. 13(6) DORA mandates ICT security awareness/resilience training as a compulsory part of staff training for ALL employees and senior management - the strongest explicit all-staff training mandate found in this project's research so far. Started as a 20-question DE/EN-only pilot (data/dora_pilot.json), same launch pattern as kyc_aml/kartellrecht/lksg. AI-drafted, NOT legally reviewed yet - see claude/dora-pilot-pre-review-dossier-2026-08-13.md for the citation ledger and confidence tiers per question. Ships free for now, same MVP posture as the rest of the catalog. scopeKind/options placeholder pattern copied verbatim from the other compliance modules.

DN-71: 10th compliance module, second cybersecurity-focused one - NIS2 (Directive (EU) 2022/2555) as transposed into the revised German BSIG ('NIS2UmsuCG'), binding since 6 Dec 2025 with no transition period, covering an estimated ~29,500 companies across 11+ sectors (energy, transport, banking, health, digital infrastructure, manufacturing, etc.). Unlike DORA, NIS2 Art. 20(2) only mandates training for management-body members personally; Art. 21(2)(g) separately requires every in-scope entity to maintain cybersecurity training as one of ten mandatory risk-management measures. Started as a 20-question DE/EN-only pilot (data/nis2_pilot.json), same launch pattern as the other enterprise compliance modules. AI-drafted, NOT legally reviewed yet - the German BSIG-specific citations (§33, §38) rest on secondary legal-analysis sources rather than a direct read of the enacted statute text; see claude/nis2-pilot-pre-review-dossier-2026-08-13.md for the full citation ledger. Ships free for now, same MVP posture as the rest of the catalog.

2026-08-15: first module from the zettacard-kb kb->JSON->staging pipeline MVP (see claude/cka-amateurfunk-kb-pipeline-mvp-2026-08-15.md and claude/cka-i18n-minimal-schema-and-translation-plan-2026-08-15.md). 131-question concept-check pilot for CKA (Certified Kubernetes Administrator) fundamentals, sourced from CNCF's curriculum (cncf/curriculum, CC-BY 4.0+), original phrasing, licensed CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 like Zettacard's other modules. AI-authored, NOT legally reviewed (not law-based content, so no counsel-review track applies the way it does for the compliance modules). IMPORTANT: the real CKA exam is 100% performance-based (live kubectl tasks against a real cluster) and is NEVER multiple-choice -- this module is honestly framed as a concept-check quiz, not an exam simulator, per explicit PO direction. First module with EN as canonical/source locale (every other module is DE-canonical) and first with a deliberately minimal 4-locale set (en/de/ja/zh) rather than the full 12 -- translations two-stage subagent translate+verify, 131/131 passed on all three non-English locales. course_ref: 'cka' on each question is a placeholder for a future hands-on course/lesson layer, not yet built. Ships free, alpha/MVP posture.
